category_title: Preschoolers with Autism and communication delays who exhibit physical aggression during activity transitions
minimal_context: Chris is in his pre-kindergarten classroom being asked to transition from playtime to a table activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Chris, it is time to clean up the toys and go to the table for our next activity.

STUDENT: No! (Drops to the floor)

TUTOR: We have to follow the schedule. Please get up.

STUDENT: (Elopes from the activity area)

TUTOR: Chris, you need to come back and transition to the table right now.

STUDENT: (Engages in physical aggression by kicking and throwing items in the classroom)

options.A: Provide simultaneous stimulation of nonverbal communication from the perspective of total communication during the student's daily classroom routines and transitions.
options.B: Start with the token board preloaded with four stickers, and when the student has three days with one behavior or less, remove one preloaded sticker.
options.C: Help the student understand the use of transition skills in different situations in real life, outside the pre-kindergarten classroom, and in other contexts.
options.D: Address the student's feelings mutually rather than repressing them, allowing for the exploration of disappointments and constraints during daily classroom transitions.
